modules.sourceReference: Day 1 Summary — Quiz Yourself, page 7; answers cross-checked with facilitator Day 1 recap
modules.title: Day 1 Knowledge Check
modules.instructions: Choose the best answer for each question. You can retake this exercise after reviewing the module.

questions.question: What are the four values of the Agile Manifesto?
questions.explanation: The Agile Manifesto values individuals and interactions, working software, customer collaboration and responding to change over their counterparts.

options.label: Individuals and interactions, working software, customer collaboration, and responding to change
Scope, schedule, cost, and quality
Planning, execution, inspection, and closure
Documentation, contracts, processes, and fixed plans

questions.question: What are the three pillars of Scrum theory?
questions.explanation: Scrum is founded on Transparency, Inspection and Adaptation.

options.label: Transparency, Inspection and Adaptation
Scope, Time and Cost
Plan, Build and Test
People, Process and Technology

questions.question: Name the five Scrum values.
questions.explanation: The five Scrum values are Commitment, Focus, Openness, Respect and Courage.

options.label: Commitment, Focus, Openness, Respect and Courage
Speed, Quality, Scope, Cost and Control
Planning, Estimation, Delivery, Review and Closure
Trust, Authority, Process, Compliance and Reporting

questions.question: What is the difference between Waterfall and Agile?
questions.explanation: Waterfall is sequential and plan-driven; Agile is iterative and incremental and welcomes feedback and change.

options.label: Waterfall is sequential; Agile is iterative and incremental
Waterfall uses teams; Agile uses only individuals
Agile prohibits planning; Waterfall requires daily planning
There is no practical difference

questions.question: Who are the three accountabilities in a Scrum Team?
questions.explanation: A Scrum Team contains one Product Owner, one Scrum Master and Developers.

options.label: Product Owner, Scrum Master and Developers
Project Manager, Business Analyst and Test Manager
Sponsor, Customer and Supplier
Architect, Team Lead and Quality Manager

modules.sourceReference: Day 2 Summary — Quiz Yourself, page 13; answers cross-checked with facilitator Day 2 recap
modules.title: Day 2 Knowledge Check
modules.instructions: Choose the best answer for each question. You can retake this exercise after reviewing the module.

questions.question: What is the Scrum Master accountable for?
questions.explanation: The Scrum Master is accountable for establishing Scrum and for the Scrum Team's effectiveness.

options.label: Establishing Scrum and enabling the Scrum Team's effectiveness
Assigning daily tasks to every Developer
Owning and ordering the Product Backlog
Approving every technical design decision

questions.question: What are the five Scrum events?
questions.explanation: The five events are the Sprint, Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review and Sprint Retrospective.

options.label: Sprint, Sprint Planning, Daily Scrum, Sprint Review and Sprint Retrospective
Charter, Planning, Execution, Control and Closure
Discovery, Design, Build, Test and Release
Backlog, Increment, Goal, Review and Deployment

questions.question: What is the purpose of the Daily Scrum?
questions.explanation: The Daily Scrum is a 15-minute event for Developers to inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt their plan.

options.label: Developers inspect progress toward the Sprint Goal and adapt their plan
The Scrum Master collects individual status reports
Stakeholders approve the Increment
The Product Owner rewrites the Product Goal

questions.question: What is the timebox for Sprint Planning?
questions.explanation: Sprint Planning is timeboxed to a maximum of eight hours for a one-month Sprint and is usually shorter for shorter Sprints.

options.label: A maximum of eight hours for a one-month Sprint
Exactly 15 minutes for every Sprint
A maximum of four hours regardless of Sprint length
There is no timebox

questions.question: What are the three topics addressed in Sprint Planning?
questions.explanation: Sprint Planning addresses why the Sprint is valuable, what can be done and how the chosen work will get done.

options.label: Why the Sprint is valuable, what can be done, and how the work will get done
Who is promoted, what the budget is, and when contracts end
What failed previously, who caused it, and who approves it
Only the exact technical solution for every backlog item

modules.sourceReference: Day 3 Summary — Quiz Yourself, page 20; answers cross-checked with facilitator artifact guidance
modules.title: Day 3 Knowledge Check
modules.instructions: Choose the best answer for each question. You can retake this exercise after reviewing the module.

questions.question: What are the three Scrum artifacts?
questions.explanation: The Scrum artifacts are the Product Backlog, Sprint Backlog and Increment.

options.label: Product Backlog, Sprint Backlog and Increment
Product Goal, Sprint Goal and Definition of Done
Charter, Schedule and Risk Register
Epic, Story and Task

questions.question: What is the Definition of Done?
questions.explanation: The Definition of Done is a formal description of the state of the Increment when it meets required quality measures.

options.label: A shared quality standard describing when an Increment is complete
A list of all future Product Backlog items
The Product Owner's approval of the Sprint plan
A deadline set by the Scrum Master

questions.question: What is the format of a user story?
questions.explanation: The common user story format is: As a [user], I want [goal], so that [benefit].

options.label: As a [user], I want [goal], so that [benefit]
Given [scope], when [cost], then [deadline]
Who, what, when, where and budget
Problem, solution, owner and status

questions.question: What is velocity used for?
questions.explanation: Velocity is an empirical planning aid used to forecast how much work a team may complete in future Sprints; it is not a cross-team performance measure.

options.label: Forecasting how much work the team may complete in future Sprints
Comparing the productivity of different Scrum Teams
Measuring the quality of the Increment
Setting the length of the Daily Scrum

questions.question: What is backlog refinement?
questions.explanation: Backlog refinement is the ongoing activity of breaking down and further defining Product Backlog items by adding details, order and size.

options.label: Ongoing clarification, decomposition, ordering and sizing of Product Backlog items
A formal Scrum event held only at the end of a Sprint
Removing every unfinished item after Sprint Review
The Scrum Master's private prioritisation meeting

modules.sourceReference: Day 4 Summary — Quiz Yourself, page 26; answers cross-checked with facilitator Day 4 recap
modules.title: Day 4 Knowledge Check
modules.instructions: Choose the best answer for each question. You can retake this exercise after reviewing the module.

questions.question: What is an impediment?
questions.explanation: An impediment is an obstacle that slows or prevents the Scrum Team from making progress or achieving its goals.

options.label: An obstacle that slows or blocks the Scrum Team's progress
Any Product Backlog item not selected for the Sprint
A stakeholder who attends Sprint Review
A change to the Sprint Backlog made by Developers

questions.question: What is the difference between coaching and telling?
questions.explanation: Coaching uses powerful questions and listening to help people think and find their own solutions; telling prescribes an answer.

options.label: Coaching helps people discover solutions; telling prescribes the solution
Coaching assigns tasks; telling removes impediments
Coaching is for managers; telling is for Scrum Masters
There is no difference

questions.question: Which set contains three facilitation techniques?
questions.explanation: Techniques such as silent brainstorming, dot voting and round-robin participation support inclusive group decisions.

options.label: Silent brainstorming, dot voting and round-robin participation
Task assignment, individual ranking and performance appraisal
Budget approval, procurement and contract review
Coding, testing and deployment

questions.question: What are the five conflict resolution approaches?
questions.explanation: The module identifies Collaborate, Compromise, Accommodate, Avoid and Compete.

options.label: Collaborate, Compromise, Accommodate, Avoid and Compete
Plan, Build, Inspect, Release and Close
Direct, Coach, Support, Delegate and Audit
Identify, Assess, Address, Follow-up and Prevent

questions.question: When should a Scrum Master escalate an impediment?
questions.explanation: Escalation is appropriate after the team cannot resolve an impediment and it lies outside the team's authority or requires organisational action.

options.label: When the team cannot resolve it and organisational authority or action is required
Immediately, before the team has tried to resolve it
Only after the Sprint has been cancelled
Never; Scrum Masters must solve every impediment alone

modules.sourceReference: Day 5 Summary — Quiz Yourself, page 31; certification facts cross-checked with facilitator Day 5 guidance
modules.title: Day 5 Knowledge Check
modules.instructions: Choose the best answer for each question. You can retake this exercise after reviewing the module.

questions.question: What is the passing score for PSM I?
questions.explanation: The Professional Scrum Master I assessment requires a score of 85% or higher.

questions.question: What is the passing score for CSM?
questions.explanation: The course booklet identifies 74% as the passing score for the Certified ScrumMaster test.

questions.question: What is the timebox for the Sprint Review?
questions.explanation: The Sprint Review is timeboxed to a maximum of four hours for a one-month Sprint and is normally shorter for shorter Sprints.

options.label: A maximum of four hours for a one-month Sprint
15 minutes for every Sprint
Eight hours for every Sprint
There is no timebox

questions.question: Who owns the Sprint Backlog?
questions.explanation: The Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers, who adapt it throughout the Sprint.

options.label: The Developers
The Scrum Master
The Product Owner
The external stakeholders

questions.question: What is the Scrum Master accountable for?
questions.explanation: The Scrum Master is accountable for establishing Scrum and enabling the effectiveness of the Scrum Team.

options.label: Establishing Scrum and enabling Scrum Team effectiveness
Managing Developers and assigning their tasks
Maximising product value by ordering the Product Backlog
Owning the Sprint Backlog and the Increment
